Page: Al-Ghazali. Sentence: Abū Ḥāmid Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad al-Ghazālī ( ; Arabic: أبو حامد محمد بن محمد الغزالي‎ ‎ ;  1058 – 19 December 1111), shortened as Al-Ghazali in Arabic or Ghazali in Persian and known as Algazelus or Algazel to the Western medieval world, was a Persian theologian, jurist, philosopher, and mystic.
Page: Averroes. Sentence: Ibn Rushd (Arabic: ‎ ‎ ; 14 April 1126 – 10 December 1198), full name (Arabic: أبو الوليد محمد ابن احمد ابن رشد‎ , "ʾAbū l-Walīd Muḥammad Ibn ʾAḥmad Ibn Rushd " ‎ ), often Latinized as Averroes ( ), was a medieval Andalusian polymath.
Page: The Incoherence of the Philosophers. Sentence: The Incoherence of the Philosophers (تهافت الفلاسفة "Tahāfut al-Falāsifaʰ" in Arabic) is the title of a landmark 11th-century work by the Persian theologian Al-Ghazali and a student of the Asharite school of Islamic theology criticizing the Avicennian school of early Islamic philosophy.

Facts:
- Abū Ḥāmid Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad al-Ghazālī was born in 1058 and died on 19 December 1111.
- Al-Ghazali was a Persian theologian, jurist, philosopher, and mystic, and he was known as Algazelus or Algazel in the Western medieval world.
- The Incoherence of the Philosophers was a landmark 11th-century work by the Persian theologian Al-Ghazali.
- The Incoherence of the Philosophers criticized the Avicennian school of early Islamic philosophy, and Al-Ghazali was a student of the Asharite school of Islamic theology.
- Ibn Rushd was born on 14 April 1126 and died on 10 December 1198.
- Ibn Rushd, often Latinized as Averroes, was a medieval Andalusian polymath.
